calls.title: Stone + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The team discussed a phased rebuild of their tracking infrastructure, transitioning from Amplitude to a real-time data pipeline using Kafka for event ingestion into Databricks. The current Amplitude setup has over 4,000 poorly defined event types, leading to governance challenges. A hybrid migration approach allows initial experimentation with a pilot group of PMs using GrowthBook, fostering growth in a culture of experimentation alongside technical development. GitHub will manage event definitions to maintain consistency, while the flexible SDK from GrowthBook enables custom integrations. Competitive pricing and ongoing organizational education efforts were also highlighted, aiming to maximize the effectiveness of experimentation and drive business value.

calls.summary: Newton Calegari (CTO at Stone) discussed migrating from Amplitude to GrowthBook's warehouse-native experimentation platform, citing pain points like event-based pricing, lack of warehouse metric support, and recent Amplitude incidents impacting feature flags and tracking. Key participants included Newton, Christian Liebenow (GrowthBook sales), and GrowthBook engineers Logan and Graham (Webflow Demo), who highlighted GrowthBook's composable architecture, open-source flexibility, API-driven design, and support for identity resolution and custom front-ends. Next steps: Newton will test GrowthBook locally via Docker, Christian will connect him with the Neon team, and they plan to reconvene in two weeks to discuss enterprise licensing and implementation.

calls.title: Stone + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The discussion centered on enhancing data infrastructure and experimentation at Stone. The team is developing a robust data pipeline to improve event tracking through distinct signal types—action, time, and business signals—while also creating an in-house experimentation platform. GrowthBook emerged as a key consideration for managing experiments and feature flags, offering modular API access and self-hosting options. Concerns about current feature flag overload, particularly with over 500 flags causing outages, prompted the shift toward GrowthBook's fail-safe design. Insights into the integration of SDKs and the asynchronous computation of metrics were also shared. The next steps involve deploying GrowthBook locally for trials and clarifying enterprise licensing options.
calls.keywords: experimentation platform, event tracking, server-side SDK, feature flags, Bayesian statistics, warehouse-native metrics
